- Use real, deterministic repository code and direct internal collaborators when practical. Do not mock

- READ: The target, minimum relevant production context, direct collaborators, and test configuration.

    full_file_path_and_name,

    return_data_type="nested_univ",
    encoding="utf-8",
    y_dtype="str",

    Data from a .ts file is loaded into a nested pd.DataFrame, or optionally into a

    multivariate problem) if requested. If present, y is loaded into a 1d np.ndarray.

       to parsing.
    return_y : boolean, default True

    return_data_type : str, optional, default = "nested_univ"
        memory data format specification to return X in.
        str can be any other supported Panel mtype
            for list of mtypes, see datatypes.SCITYPE_REGISTER
            for specifications, see examples/AA_datatypes_and_datasets.ipynb

def write_dataframe_to_tsfile(
    data,
    path,
    problem_name="sample_data",
    class_label=None,
    class_value_list=None,
    equal_length=False,
    series_length=-1,
    missing_values="NaN",
    comment=None,
    fold="",
):
    """Output a dataset in dataframe format to .ts file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data: pandas dataframe
        The dataset in a dataframe to be written as a ts file
        which must be of the structure specified in the documentation
        examples/loading_data.ipynb.
        index |   dim_0   |   dim_1   |    ...    |  dim_c-1
           0  | pd.Series | pd.Series | pd.Series | pd.Series
           1  | pd.Series | pd.Series | pd.Series | pd.Series
          ... |    ...    |    ...    |    ...    |    ...
           n  | pd.Series | pd.Series | pd.Series | pd.Series
    path: str
        The full path to output the ts file to.
    problem_name: str, default="sample_data"
        The problemName to print in the header of the ts file and also the name of
        the file.
    class_label: list of str or None, default=None
        The problems class labels to show the possible class values for in the file
        header, optional.
    class_value_list: list, ndarray or None, default=None
        The class values for each case, optional.
    equal_length: bool, default=False
        Indicates whether each series is of equal length.
    series_length: int, default=-1
        Indicates the series length if they are of equal length.
    missing_values: str, default="NaN"
        Representation for missing values.
    comment: str or None, default=None
        Comment text to be inserted before the header in a block.
    fold: str or None, default=None
        Addon at the end of the filename, i.e. _TRAIN or _TEST.

    Returns
    -------
    None

    Notes
    -----
    This version currently does not support writing timestamp data.
    """
    # ensure data provided is a dataframe
    if not isinstance(data, pd.DataFrame):
        raise ValueError(f"Data provided must be a DataFrame, passed a {type(data)}")
    data_valid, _, metadata = check_is_scitype(
        data, scitype="Panel", return_metadata=True
    )
    if not data_valid:
        raise ValueError("DataFrame provided is not a valid type")
    if equal_length != metadata["is_equal_length"]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Argument passed for equal length = {equal_length} is not "
            f"true for the data passed"
        )
    if equal_length:
        # Convert to [cases][dimensions][length] numpy.
        data = convert_to(
            data,
            to_type="numpy3D",
            as_scitype="Panel",
            store_behaviour="freeze",
        )
        write_ndarray_to_tsfile(
            data,
            path,
            problem_name=problem_name,
            class_label=class_label,
            class_value_list=class_value_list,
            equal_length=equal_length,
            series_length=data.shape[2],
            missing_values=missing_values,
            comment=comment,
            fold=fold,
        )
    else:  # Write by iterating over dataframe
        if class_value_list is not None and class_label is None:
            class_label = np.unique(class_value_list)
        file = _write_header(
            path,
            problem_name,
            metadata["is_univariate"],
            metadata["is_equal_length"],
            series_length,
            class_label,
            fold,
            comment,
        )
        n_cases, n_dimensions = data.shape
        for i in range(0, n_cases):
            for j in range(0, n_dimensions):
                series = data.iloc[i, j]
                for k in range(0, series.size - 1):
                    file.write(f"{series[k]},")
                file.write(f"{series[series.size - 1]}:")
            file.write(f"{class_value_list[i]}\n")

    if not isinstance(data, np.ndarray):

    if class_value_list is not None:

    if class_value_list is not None and class_label is None:
        class_label = np.unique(class_value_list)
    elif class_value_list is None:

    # ensure number of cases is same as the class value list
    if len(data) != len(class_value_list) and len(class_value_list) > 0:

            "The number of cases is not the same as the number of given class values"

        equal_length,
        series_length,
        class_label,

    # which are the series and the class value list if there is any
    for case, value in itertools.zip_longest(data, class_value_list):

            if not univariate:

        elif class_label is not None:
            file.write(f"{a}{missing_values}")

def _write_header(
    path,
    problem_name,
    univariate,
    equal_length,
    series_length,
    class_label,
    fold,
    comment,
):
    """Write the header information for a ts file."""
    # create path if not exist
    dirt = f"{str(path)}/{str(problem_name)}/"
    try:
        os.makedirs(dirt)
    except OSError:
        pass  # raises os.error if path already exists
    # create ts file in the path
    file = open(f"{dirt}{str(problem_name)}{fold}.ts", "w")
    # write comment if any as a block at start of file
    if comment is not None:
        file.write("\n# ".join(textwrap.wrap("# " + comment)))
        file.write("\n")

    """ Writes the header info for a ts file"""
    file.write(f"@problemName {problem_name}\n")
    file.write("@timestamps false\n")
    file.write(f"@univariate {str(univariate).lower()}\n")
    file.write(f"@equalLength {str(equal_length).lower()}\n")
    if series_length > 0 and equal_length:
        file.write(f"@seriesLength {series_length}\n")
    # write class label line
    if class_label is not None:
        space_separated_class_label = " ".join(str(label) for label in class_label)
        file.write(f"@classLabel true {space_separated_class_label}\n")
    else:
        file.write("@classLabel false\n")
    file.write("@data\n")
    return file

        written directly to the directory passed in output_path
    y_true : np.array, default = None
        Actual values, written to file with the predicted values if present
    predicted_probs :  np.ndarray, default = None

    split : str, default = "TEST"

    second_line : str
        unstructured, used for predictor parameters
    third_line : str

"""Tests for reading and writing the .ts time-series file format."""

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from sktime.datasets._readers_writers.ts import (
    load_from_tsfile,
    load_from_tsfile_to_dataframe,
    write_dataframe_to_tsfile,
    write_ndarray_to_tsfile,
    write_panel_to_tsfile,
)


def _write_text(path, contents, encoding="utf-8"):
    """Write a small .ts file and return its path."""
    path.write_text(contents, encoding=encoding)
    return path


def _classification_file(tmp_path, data_lines, *, multivariate=False, name="sample.ts"):
    """Create a basic labelled .ts file for reader tests."""
    header = (
        "@problemName Sample\n"
        "@timestamps false\n"
        f"@univariate {'false' if multivariate else 'true'}\n"
        "@classLabel true A B\n"
        "@data\n"
    )
    return _write_text(tmp_path / name, header + data_lines)


def _nested_panel(*, equal_length):
    """Return a small nested-univ panel, optionally with unequal lengths."""
    if equal_length:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "dim_0": [pd.Series([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]), pd.Series([4.0, 5.0, 6.0])],
                "dim_1": [pd.Series([10.0, 20.0, 30.0]), pd.Series([40.0, 50.0, 60.0])],
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "dim_0": [pd.Series([1.0, 2.0]), pd.Series([3.0, 4.0, 5.0])],
            "dim_1": [pd.Series([10.0]), pd.Series([20.0, 30.0, 40.0])],
        }
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# load_from_tsfile_to_dataframe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_load_to_dataframe_returns_separate_x_and_y(tmp_path):
    path = _classification_file(tmp_path, "1,2,3:A\n\n4,5,6:B\n")

    X, y = load_from_tsfile_to_dataframe(path)

    assert isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame)
    assert list(X.columns) == ["dim_0"]
    assert X["dim_0"].iloc[0].tolist() == [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
    assert X["dim_0"].iloc[1].tolist() == [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]
    assert isinstance(y, np.ndarray)
    assert y.tolist() == ["a", "b"]


def test_load_to_dataframe_can_return_combined_x_and_y(tmp_path):
    path = _classification_file(tmp_path, "1,2:A\n3,4:B\n")

    result = load_from_tsfile_to_dataframe(path, return_separate_X_and_y=False)

    assert isinstance(result, pd.DataFrame)
    assert list(result.columns) == ["dim_0", "class_vals"]
    assert result["dim_0"].iloc[0].tolist() == [1.0, 2.0]
    assert result["class_vals"].tolist() == ["a", "b"]


def test_load_to_dataframe_multivariate_data(tmp_path):
    path = _classification_file(
        tmp_path,
        "1,2:10,20:A\n3,4,5:30,40,50:B\n",
        multivariate=True,
    )

    X, y = load_from_tsfile_to_dataframe(path)

"""Tests for reading and writing the .ts time-series file format."""

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from sktime.datasets._readers_writers.ts import (
    load_from_tsfile,
    load_from_tsfile_to_dataframe,
    write_dataframe_to_tsfile,
    write_ndarray_to_tsfile,
    write_panel_to_tsfile,
)


def _write_text(path, contents, encoding="utf-8"):
    """Write a small .ts file and return its path."""
    path.write_text(contents, encoding=encoding)
    return path


def _classification_file(tmp_path, data_lines, *, multivariate=False, name="sample.ts"):
    """Create a basic labelled .ts file for reader tests."""
    header = (
        "@problemName Sample\n"
        "@timestamps false\n"
        f"@univariate {'false' if multivariate else 'true'}\n"
        "@classLabel true A B\n"
        "@data\n"
    )
    return _write_text(tmp_path / name, header + data_lines)


def _nested_panel(*, equal_length):
    """Return a small nested-univ panel, optionally with unequal lengths."""
    if equal_length:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "dim_0": [pd.Series([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]), pd.Series([4.0, 5.0, 6.0])],
                "dim_1": [pd.Series([10.0, 20.0, 30.0]), pd.Series([40.0, 50.0, 60.0])],
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "dim_0": [pd.Series([1.0, 2.0]), pd.Series([3.0, 4.0, 5.0])],
            "dim_1": [pd.Series([10.0]), pd.Series([20.0, 30.0, 40.0])],
        }
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# load_from_tsfile_to_dataframe
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_load_to_dataframe_returns_separate_x_and_y(tmp_path):
    path = _classification_file(tmp_path, "1,2,3:A\n\n4,5,6:B\n")

    X, y = load_from_tsfile_to_dataframe(path)

    assert isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame)
    assert list(X.columns) == ["dim_0"]
    assert X["dim_0"].iloc[0].tolist() == [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
    assert X["dim_0"].iloc[1].tolist() == [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]
    assert isinstance(y, np.ndarray)
    assert y.tolist() == ["a", "b"]

    assert isinstance(result, pd.DataFrame)
    assert list(result.columns) == ["dim_0", "class_vals"]
    assert result["dim_0"].iloc[0].tolist() == [1.0, 2.0]
    assert result["class_vals"].tolist() == ["a", "b"]

def _write_text(path, contents, encoding="utf-8"):
    """Write a small .ts file and return its path."""
    path.write_text(contents, encoding=encoding)
    return path


def _classification_file(tmp_path, data_lines, *, multivariate=False, name="sample.ts"):
    """Create a basic labelled .ts file for reader tests."""
    header = (
        "@problemName Sample\n"
        "@timestamps false\n"
        f"@univariate {'false' if multivariate else 'true'}\n"
        "@classLabel true A B\n"
        "@data\n"
    )
    return _write_text(tmp_path / name, header + data_lines)


def _nested_panel(*, equal_length):
    """Return a small nested-univ panel, optionally with unequal lengths."""
    if equal_length:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "dim_0": [pd.Series([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]), pd.Series([4.0, 5.0, 6.0])],
                "dim_1": [pd.Series([10.0, 20.0, 30.0]), pd.Series([40.0, 50.0, 60.0])],
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "dim_0": [pd.Series([1.0, 2.0]), pd.Series([3.0, 4.0, 5.0])],
            "dim_1": [pd.Series([10.0]), pd.Series([20.0, 30.0, 40.0])],

    def metrics_by_strategy(self):

    def metrics_by_strategy_dataset(self):

    def plot_boxplots(self, metric_name=None, **kwargs):
        """Box plot of metric."""
        _check_soft_dependencies("matplotlib")

        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402

        plt.style.use("seaborn-ticks")

        self._check_is_evaluated()
        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)
        column = self._get_column_name(metric_name, suffix="mean")

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1)
        self.metrics_by_strategy_dataset.boxplot(
            by="strategy", column=column, grid=False, ax=ax, **kwargs
        )

        )

    def rank(self, metric_name=None, ascending=False):
        """Determine estimator ranking.

        Calculates the average ranks based on the performance of each estimator on each
        dataset
        """

        if not isinstance(ascending, bool):
            raise ValueError(
                f"`ascending` must be boolean, but found: {type(ascending)}"
            )

        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)
        column = self._get_column_name(metric_name, suffix="mean")

        ranked = (
            self.metrics_by_strategy_dataset.loc[:, ["dataset", "strategy", column]]
            .set_index("strategy")
            .groupby("dataset")
            .rank(ascending=ascending)
            .reset_index()
            .groupby("strategy")
            .mean()
            .rename(columns={column: f"{metric_name}_mean_rank"})
            .reset_index()

    def t_test(self, metric_name=None):

        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)
        metrics_per_estimator_dataset = self._get_metrics_per_estimator_dataset(
            metric_name
        )

        t_df = pd.DataFrame()
        perms = itertools.product(metrics_per_estimator_dataset.keys(), repeat=2)
        values = np.array([])
        for perm in perms:
            x = np.array(metrics_per_estimator_dataset[perm[0]])
            y = np.array(metrics_per_estimator_dataset[perm[1]])
            t_stat, p_val = ttest_ind(x, y)

            t_test = {
                "estimator_1": perm[0],
                "estimator_2": perm[1],
                "t_stat": t_stat,
                "p_val": p_val,
            }

            t_df = pd.concat([t_df, pd.DataFrame(t_test, index=[0])], ignore_index=True)
            values = np.append(values, t_stat)
            values = np.append(values, p_val)

        index = t_df["estimator_1"].unique()
        values_names = ["t_stat", "p_val"]
        col_idx = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([index, values_names])
        values_reshaped = values.reshape(len(index), len(values_names) * len(index))

        values_df_multiindex = pd.DataFrame(
            values_reshaped, index=index, columns=col_idx
        )

        return t_df, values_df_multiindex

    def sign_test(self, metric_name=None):
        """Non-parametric test for consistent differences between observation pairs.

        See `<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sign_test>`_ for details about
        the test and
        `<https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-0.14.0/reference/generated/scipy
        .stats.binom_test.html>`_
        for details about the scipy implementation.
        """
        self._check_is_evaluated()
        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)
        metrics_per_estimator_dataset = self._get_metrics_per_estimator_dataset(
            metric_name
        )

        sign_df = pd.DataFrame()
        perms = itertools.product(metrics_per_estimator_dataset.keys(), repeat=2)

        for perm in perms:
            x = np.array(metrics_per_estimator_dataset[perm[0]])
            y = np.array(metrics_per_estimator_dataset[perm[1]])
            signs = np.sum([i[0] > i[1] for i in zip(x, y)])
            n = len(x)

                binom = stats.binomtest
            else:

            sign_df = pd.concat(
                [sign_df, pd.DataFrame(sign_test, index=[0])], ignore_index=True

            sign_df_pivot = sign_df.pivot(

        The test counts the number of observations that are greater, smaller
        and equal to the mean
        `<http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilcoxon_rank-sum_test>`_.
        """

            x = metrics_per_estimator_dataset[perm[0]]
            y = metrics_per_estimator_dataset[perm[1]]
            t_stat, p_val = ranksums(x, y)
            ranksum = {
                "estimator_1": perm[0],
                "estimator_2": perm[1],
                "t_stat": t_stat,
                "p_val": p_val,
            }
            ranksum_df = pd.concat(
                [ranksum_df, pd.DataFrame(ranksum, index=[0])], ignore_index=True
            )

            values = np.append(values, p_val)

        self._check_is_evaluated()
        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)

        df_t_test, _ = self.t_test(metric_name=metric_name)
        idx_estim_1 = df_t_test["estimator_1"].unique()
        idx_estim_2 = df_t_test["estimator_2"].unique()
        estim_1 = len(idx_estim_1)
        estim_2 = len(idx_estim_2)
        critical_value = alpha / (estim_1 * estim_2)

        bonfer_test = df_t_test["p_val"] <= critical_value

        bonfer_test_reshaped = bonfer_test.values.reshape(estim_1, estim_2)

        bonfer_df = pd.DataFrame(

    def wilcoxon_test(self, metric_name=None):
        """Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

        http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilcoxon_signed-rank_test
        `Wilcoxon signed-rank test
        <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilcoxon_signed-rank_test>`_.
        Tests whether two  related paired samples come from the same
        distribution. In particular, it tests whether the distribution of the
        differences x-y is symmetric about zero
        """
        self._check_is_evaluated()
        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)
        metrics_per_estimator_dataset = self._get_metrics_per_estimator_dataset(
            metric_name
        )

        wilcoxon_df = pd.DataFrame()
        prod = itertools.combinations(metrics_per_estimator_dataset.keys(), 2)
        for p in prod:
            estim_1 = p[0]
            estim_2 = p[1]
            w, p_val = stats.wilcoxon(
                metrics_per_estimator_dataset[p[0]], metrics_per_estimator_dataset[p[1]]
            )

            w_test = {
                "estimator_1": estim_1,
                "estimator_2": estim_2,
                "statistic": w,
                "p_val": p_val,
            }

            wilcoxon_df = pd.concat(
                [wilcoxon_df, pd.DataFrame(w_test, index=[0])], ignore_index=True
            )

        return wilcoxon_df

    def friedman_test(self, metric_name=None):
        """Friedman test.

        The Friedman test is a non-parametric statistical test used to
        detect differences
        in treatments across multiple test attempts. The procedure involves
        ranking each row (or block) together,
        then considering the values of ranks by columns.
        Implementation used:
        `scipy.stats <https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy-0.15.1/reference
        /generated/scipy.stats.friedmanchisquare.html>`_.
        """
        self._check_is_evaluated()
        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)
        metrics_per_estimator_dataset = self._get_metrics_per_estimator_dataset(
            metric_name
        )

        friedman_test = stats.friedmanchisquare(
            *[
                metrics_per_estimator_dataset[k]
                for k in metrics_per_estimator_dataset.keys()
            ]
        )
        values = [friedman_test[0], friedman_test[1]]
        values_df = pd.DataFrame([values], columns=["statistic", "p_value"])

        return friedman_test, values_df

    def nemenyi(self, metric_name=None):
        """Nemenyi test.

        Post-hoc test run if the `friedman_test` reveals statistical significance. For
        more information see
        `Nemenyi test <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemenyi_test>`_.
         Implementation used `scikit-posthocs
        <https://github.com/maximtrp/scikit-posthocs>`_.
        """
        _check_soft_dependencies("scikit_posthocs")

        # lazy import to avoid hard dependency
        from scikit_posthocs import posthoc_nemenyi

        self._check_is_evaluated()
        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)
        metrics_per_estimator_dataset = self._get_metrics_per_estimator_dataset(
            metric_name
        )

        strategy_dict = pd.DataFrame(metrics_per_estimator_dataset)
        strategy_dict = strategy_dict.melt(var_name="groups", value_name="values")
        nemenyi = posthoc_nemenyi(strategy_dict, val_col="values", group_col="groups")
        return nemenyi

    def fit_runtime(self, unit="s", train_or_test="test", cv_fold="all"):
        """Calculate the average time for fitting the strategy.

        Parameters
        ----------
        unit : string (must be either 's' for seconds, 'm' for minutes or 'h' for hours)
            the unit in which the run time will be calculated

        Returns
        -------
        run_times: Pandas DataFrame
            average run times per estimator and strategy
        """
        # check input
        if isinstance(cv_fold, int) and cv_fold >= 0:
            cv_folds = [cv_fold]  # if single fold, make iterable
        elif cv_fold == "all":
            cv_folds = np.arange(self.results.cv.get_n_splits())
            if len(cv_folds) == 0:
                raise ValueError()
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"`cv_fold` must be either positive integer (>=0) or 'all', "
                f"but found: {type(cv_fold)}"
            )

        # load all predictions
        run_times_frames = []
        for cv_fold in cv_folds:
            for result in self.results.load_predictions(
                cv_fold=cv_fold, train_or_test=train_or_test
            ):
                # unwrap result object
                strategy_name = result.strategy_name
                dataset_name = result.dataset_name
                fit_estimator_start_time = result.fit_estimator_start_time
                fit_estimator_end_time = result.fit_estimator_end_time
                predict_estimator_start_time = result.predict_estimator_start_time
                predict_estimator_end_time = result.predict_estimator_end_time
                unwrapped = pd.DataFrame(
                    {
                        "strategy_name": [strategy_name],
                        "dataset_name": [dataset_name],
                        "fit_estimator_start_time": [fit_estimator_start_time],
                        "fit_estimator_end_time": [fit_estimator_end_time],
                        "predict_estimator_start_time": [predict_estimator_start_time],
                        "predict_estimator_end_time": [predict_estimator_end_time],
                        "cv_fold": [cv_fold],
                    }
                )
                run_times_frames.append(unwrapped)
        run_times = pd.concat(run_times_frames, ignore_index=True)

        # calculate run time difference
        run_times["fit_runtime"] = (
            run_times["fit_estimator_end_time"] - run_times["fit_estimator_start_time"]
        ) / np.timedelta64(1, unit)
        run_times["predict_runtime"] = (
            run_times["predict_estimator_end_time"]
            - run_times["predict_estimator_start_time"]
        ) / np.timedelta64(1, unit)

        return pd.pivot_table(
            run_times,
            index=["strategy_name", "dataset_name"],
            values=["fit_runtime", "predict_runtime"],
            aggfunc={"fit_runtime": np.average, "predict_runtime": np.average},

    def _get_column_name(self, metric_name, suffix="mean"):

    def _check_is_evaluated(self):
        """Check if evaluator has evaluated any metrics."""
        if len(self._metric_names) == 0:
            raise NotEvaluatedError(
                "This evaluator has not evaluated any metric yet. Please call "
                "'evaluate' with the appropriate arguments before using this "
                "method."
            )

    def _validate_metric_name(self, metric_name):
        """Check if metric has already been evaluated."""
        if metric_name is None:
            metric_name = self._metric_names[
                -1
            ]  # if None, use the last evaluated metric

        if metric_name not in self._metric_names:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{metric_name} has not been evaluated yet. Please call "
                f"'evaluate' with the appropriate arguments first"
            )

        return metric_name

        df = self.metrics_by_strategy_dataset.loc[:, columns]
        d = {}
        for dataset in df.dataset.unique():
            results = []
            for strategy in df.strategy.unique():
                row = df.loc[(df.strategy == strategy) & (df.dataset == dataset), :]
                m = row["accuracy_mean"].values[0]

                results.append([strategy, m, s])
            d[dataset] = results
        return d

        metric_name = self._validate_metric_name(metric_name)

        ranked = (

            .groupby("dataset")
            .rank(ascending=ascending)
            .reset_index()
            .groupby("strategy")
            .mean()
            .rename(columns={column: f"{metric_name}_mean_rank"})
            .reset_index()
        )
        return ranked

class HDDBaseResults(BaseResults):

    def __init__(self, path):
        # validate paths
        self._validate_path(path)

        # set path
        self._path = path

        super().__init__()

    @property
    def path(self):
        """Path for results on HDD."""
        return self._path

    def save(self):
        """Save results object as master file."""
        from joblib import dump, load

        file = os.path.join(self.path, "results.pickle")

        # if file does not exist already, create a new one
        if not os.path.isfile(file):
            dump(self, file)

        # if file already exists, update file adding new datasets,
        # strategies and/or cv_folds
        else:
            results = load(file)
            self.strategy_names = list(
                set(self.strategy_names + results.strategy_names)
            )
            self.dataset_names = list(set(self.dataset_names + results.dataset_names))
            dump(self, file)

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_path(path):
        """Validate paths."""
        # check if path already exists
        if os.path.exists(path):
            if not os.path.isdir(path):
                raise ValueError("path already exists and is not a directory")

            elif os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path, "results.pickle")):
                warn(
                    f"Existing results file found in given path: {path}. "
                    f"Results file will be updated"
                )

            elif (
                len([file for file in os.listdir(path) if not file.startswith(".")]) > 0
            ):
                warn("path already exists and is not empty")

from warnings import warn

import numpy as np

from sktime.benchmarking.base import _V1_DEPRECATION_MSG, BaseMetric


class PairwiseMetric(BaseMetric):
    """Compute metric pairwise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    func : function
        Function that computes the pairwise metric.

    name : str
        Name of the metric
    """

    def __init__(self, func, name=None, **kwargs):
        warn(_V1_DEPRECATION_MSG, FutureWarning, stacklevel=2)
        name = func.__name__ if name is None else name
        self.func = func
        super().__init__(name=name, **kwargs)

    def compute(self, y_true, y_pred):
        """Compute metric and standard error."""
        # compute mean
        mean = self.func(y_true, y_pred)

        # compute stderr based on pairwise metrics
        n_instances = len(y_true)
        pointwise_metrics = np.array(
            [self.func([y_true[i]], [y_pred[i]]) for i in range(n_instances)]
        )
        stderr = np.std(pointwise_metrics) / np.sqrt(
            n_instances - 1
        )  # sample standard error of the mean

        return mean, stderr

    """Compute metric pairwise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    func : function
        Function that computes the pairwise metric.

    name : str
        Name of the metric
    """

        warn(_V1_DEPRECATION_MSG, FutureWarning, stacklevel=2)
        allowed_methods = ("jackknife",)
        if method not in allowed_methods:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"Provided method is not implemented yet. "
                f"Currently only: {allowed_methods} are implemented"
            )
        self.method = method

        name = func.__name__ if name is None else name
        self.func = func

        super().__init__(name=name, **kwargs)

    def compute(self, y_true, y_pred):
        """Compute metric and standard error.

        References
        ----------
        .. [1] Efron and Stein, (1981), "The jackknife estimate of variance."

        .. [2] McIntosh, Avery. "The Jackknife Estimation Method".
            <http://people.bu.edu/aimcinto/jackknife.pdf>

        .. [3] Efron, Bradley. "The Jackknife, the Bootstrap, and other
            Resampling Plans". Technical Report No. 63, Division of
            Biostatistics,
            Stanford University, December, 1980.

        .. [4] Jackknife resampling
        <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackknife_resampling>
        """
        # compute aggregate metric
        mean = self.func(y_true, y_pred, **self.kwargs)

        # compute stderr based on jackknifed metrics

    "off" = runs tests for all estimators

if multiple options are turned on, they are combined with AND,

"""

Design principal fixture: `evaluator` building 2 strategies × 2 datasets × 2 folds where strategy s1 errors: fold0 → 1 (metric 0.25), etc. Let me carefully design data so expected values are easy:

s1 error magnitudes constant: y_pred = [1,2,3,5] → mae=0.25 per fold/dataset regardless.
s2 y_pred = [2,2,2,2] → mae = (1+0+1+2)/4 = 1.0.

To create variety across folds for rank tests, better have per-fold values differing: e.g., for dataset d1: s1 mae 0.25, s2 1.0; dataset d2: s1 1.5, s2 0.5. Then rank over 2 datasets: for d1, s1 rank 2 (ascending False → rank 1 = highest) etc. Let's plan a design where rank gives non-trivial fractions.

Simplify: define per (dataset, fold, strategy) predictions with a deterministic generator:

pred[dataset][strategy] = y_pred arrays such that mae values are prescribed. Easiest: y_true = zeros of length 4? MAE of constant y_pred = |y_pred| if y_true zero. Use y_true = np.zeros(4) and y_pred = np.full(4, value) → mae = |value|, stderr = 0. Hmm stderr=0 for constant offsets (pointwise metrics all same). That's fine and simple, but stderr 0 in rank doesn't matter.

But using y_true zeros is a bit degenerate. Alternative: y_true = np.array([1.,2.,3.,4.]) and y_pred = y_true + offset → mae = |offset| and stderr = 0. That's clean: metric value exactly equals |offset|. But stderr = 0 makes `metrics_by_strategy_dataset` mae_stderr 0 — for statistical tests with zero variance, t-tests yield NaN/inf. I earlier saw inf for differing constant arrays. That would break meaningful assertions for t_test.

Better: use mixed predictions so stderr nonzero, and compute expected metrics independently with actual numpy computation in the test (not re-implementing evaluate; computing 0.25 = mean abs diff is fine and meaningful).

function.arguments:
{"command": "mkdir -p /testbed/tests/sktime/benchmarking && cat > /testbed/tests/sktime/benchmarking/test_evaluation.py <<'PYEOF'
"""Tests for ``sktime.benchmarking.evaluation.Evaluator``.

The tests exercise the externally visible behaviour of the deprecated v1
``Evaluator``: metric computation, the aggregated result frames, the ranking
and statistical test helpers, run time aggregation, and the plotting entry
points.  Real repository collaborators (``RAMResults``, ``PairwiseMetric``)
are used throughout; only the (fixed) seed data, the cross validation
splitter and, where unavoidable, the plotting backends are controlled.
"""

import importlib.util
import itertools
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from sktime.benchmarking.evaluation import Evaluator
from sktime.benchmarking.metrics import PairwiseMetric
from sktime.benchmarking.results import RAMResults
from sktime.exceptions import NotEvaluatedError

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# deterministic fixture data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Y_TRUE = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])

STRATEGIES = ("s1", "s2", "s3")
DATASETS = ("d1", "d2")
FOLDS = (0, 1)

# predictions per (strategy, dataset), one array per cv fold
PREDICTIONS = {
    ("s1", "d1"): [[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 6.0]],
    ("s1", "d2"): [[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], [2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0]],
    ("s2", "d1"): [[2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0], [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]],
    ("s2", "d2"): [[1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 3.0], [2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0]],
    ("s3", "d1"): [[1.5, 3.0, 4.0, 4.5], [2.0, 3.5, 4.5, 5.0]],
    ("s3", "d2"): [[2.0, 3.5, 4.5, 5.0], [1.5, 3.0, 4.0, 4.5]],
}

# hand-computed mean absolute error of the predictions above, per fold
EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD = {
    ("s1", "d1"): (0.0, 0.5),
    ("s1", "d2"): (0.0, 1.0),
    ("s2", "d1"): (1.0, 1.5),
    ("s2", "d2"): (0.5, 1.0),
    ("s3", "d1"): (0.75, 1.25),
    ("s3", "d2"): (1.25, 0.75),
}

# hand-computed average of the fold values above
EXPECTED_MAE_PER_DATASET = {
    key: float(np.mean(values)) for key, values in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD.items()
}

# hand-computed average of the per-dataset values above
EXPECTED_MAE_PER_STRATEGY = {
    strategy: float(
        np.mean(
            [
                EXPECTED_MAE_PER_DATASET[(strategy, dataset)]
                for dataset in DATASETS
            ]
        )
    )
    for strategy in STRATEGIES
}

# hand-computed mean absolute error of the max-absolute-error metric, per fold
EXPECTED_MAXAE_PER_DATASET = {
    ("s1", "d1"): 1.0,
    ("s1", "d2"): 0.5,
    ("s2", "d1"): 2.5,
    ("s2", "d2"): 0.5,
    ("s3", "d1"): 1.25,
    ("s3", "d2"): 1.25,
}

FIT_SECONDS = {0: 10.0, 1: 20.0}
PREDICT_SECONDS = {0: 5.0, 1: 10.0}
MEAN_FIT_SECONDS = float(np.mean(list(FIT_SECONDS.values())))
MEAN_PREDICT_SECONDS = float(np.mean(list(PREDICT_SECONDS.values())))

# constant predictions used for the "train" split, MAE with Y_TRUE is 2.5
TRAIN_Y_PRED = np.zeros(4)
TRAIN_MAE = 2.5


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class _FixedCV:
    """Minimal deterministic stand-in for a cross validation splitter."""

    def __init__(self, n_splits):
        self._n_splits = n_splits

    def get_n_splits(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return self._n_splits


def _mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred):
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(y_true - y_pred)))


def _max_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred):
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    return float(np.max(np.abs(y_true - y_pred)))


def _build_results(
    strategies=STRATEGIES,
    datasets=DATASETS,
    folds=FOLDS,
    n_splits=2,
    with_train=False,
):
    """Build an in-memory ``RAMResults`` with deterministic predictions."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        results = RAMResults()
    results.cv = _FixedCV(n_splits=n_splits)

    for strategy, dataset in itertools.product(strategies, datasets):
        for fold in folds:
            fit_start = pd.Timestamp("2020-01-01 00:00:00")
            fit_end = fit_start + pd.Timedelta(seconds=FIT_SECONDS[fold])
            predict_start = fit_end
            predict_end = predict_start + pd.Timedelta(seconds=PREDICT_SECONDS[fold])
            timings = {
                "fit_estimator_start_time": fit_start,
                "fit_estimator_end_time": fit_end,
                "predict_estimator_start_time": predict_start,
                "predict_estimator_end_time": predict_end,
            }
            with warnings.catch_warnings():
                warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
                results.save_predictions(
                    strategy_name=strategy,
                    dataset_name=dataset,
                    y_true=Y_TRUE,
                    y_pred=np.array(PREDICTIONS[(strategy, dataset)][fold]),
                    y_proba=None,
                    index=np.arange(len(Y_TRUE)),
                    cv_fold=fold,
                    train_or_test="test",
                    **timings,
                )
                if with_train:
                    results.save_predictions(
                        strategy_name=strategy,
                        dataset_name=dataset,
                        y_true=Y_TRUE,
                        y_pred=TRAIN_Y_PRED,
                        y_proba=None,
                        index=np.arange(len(Y_TRUE)),
                        cv_fold=fold,
                        train_or_test="train",
                        **timings,
                    )
    return results


def _new_evaluator(results):
    """Create an ``Evaluator`` without surfacing the deprecation warning."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        return Evaluator(results)


def _mae_metric():
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        return PairwiseMetric(func=_mean_absolute_error, name="mae")


def _maxae_metric():
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        return PairwiseMetric(func=_max_absolute_error, name="maxae")


@pytest.fixture
def results():
    """In-memory results for three strategies, two datasets and two folds."""
    return _build_results()


@pytest.fixture
def raw_evaluator(results):
    """Evaluator that has not computed any metric yet."""
    return _new_evaluator(results)


@pytest.fixture
def evaluator(results):
    """Evaluator with the ``mae`` metric computed on all folds."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric())
    return ev


@pytest.fixture
def plot_backend(monkeypatch):
    """Run the legacy plotting helpers on current matplotlib/numpy.

    ``plot_boxplots`` asks for the ``seaborn-ticks`` style which matplotlib
    renamed to ``seaborn-v0_8-ticks`` and the critical difference diagram
    relies on ``numpy.asfarray`` which was removed in numpy 2.  Both are
    external compatibility shims, not changes to the behaviour under test.
    """
    matplotlib = pytest.importorskip("matplotlib")
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    legacy_style_use = plt.style.use

    def _style_use(style):
        if style == "seaborn-ticks" and style not in plt.style.available:
            style = "seaborn-v0_8-ticks"
        return legacy_style_use(style)

    monkeypatch.setattr(plt.style, "use", _style_use)
    if not hasattr(np, "asfarray"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(np, "asfarray", np.asarray, raising=False)
    yield plt
    plt.close("all")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# construction and validation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_evaluator_requires_base_results():
    """Passing a non-``BaseResults`` object is rejected."""
    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="must inherit from BaseResults"):
            Evaluator(results=[1, 2, 3])


def test_evaluator_emits_v1_deprecation_warning():
    """The deprecated v1 evaluator warns on construction."""
    res = _build_results()
    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning, match="deprecated"):
        ev = Evaluator(res)
    assert ev.results is res


def test_metric_names_is_empty_before_evaluation(raw_evaluator):
    """``metric_names`` is readable (and empty) on an unevaluated evaluator."""
    assert raw_evaluator.metric_names == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "attribute",
    ["metrics", "metrics_by_strategy", "metrics_by_strategy_dataset"],
)
def test_metrics_properties_require_evaluation(raw_evaluator, attribute):
    """Accessing aggregated frames before ``evaluate`` raises."""
    with pytest.raises(NotEvaluatedError, match="has not evaluated any metric"):
        getattr(raw_evaluator, attribute)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# evaluate
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_evaluate_returns_aggregated_metrics_by_strategy(evaluator):
    """``evaluate`` returns (and exposes) the per-strategy aggregation."""
    aggregated = evaluator.metrics_by_strategy

    pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(aggregated, evaluator.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric()))

    assert list(aggregated.columns) == ["strategy", "mae_mean", "mae_stderr"]
    assert set(aggregated["strategy"]) == set(STRATEGIES)
    assert evaluator.metric_names == ["mae"]


def test_evaluate_aggregates_metric_values_per_strategy(evaluator):
    """Per-strategy metric values are the mean over datasets and folds."""
    aggregated = evaluator.metrics_by_strategy.set_index("strategy")
    for strategy, expected in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_STRATEGY.items():
        assert aggregated.loc[strategy, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_evaluate_records_one_row_per_strategy_dataset_and_fold(evaluator):
    """Raw per-fold metrics are stored with the documented columns."""
    metrics = evaluator.metrics

    assert list(metrics.columns) == [
        "dataset",
        "strategy",
        "cv_fold",
        "mae_mean",
        "mae_stderr",
    ]
    assert len(metrics) == len(STRATEGIES) * len(DATASETS) * len(FOLDS)

    for (strategy, dataset), per_fold in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD.items():
        rows = metrics[
            (metrics["strategy"] == strategy) & (metrics["dataset"] == dataset)
        ].set_index("cv_fold")
        for fold, expected in enumerate(per_fold):
            assert rows.loc[fold, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_evaluate_stores_non_negative_standard_errors(evaluator):
    """The ``stderr`` companion column is populated for every fold."""
    stderrs = evaluator.metrics["mae_stderr"]
    assert stderrs.notna().all()
    assert (stderrs >= 0).all()
    # the degenerate fold with a perfect forecast has zero error spread
    perfect = evaluator.metrics[
        (evaluator.metrics["strategy"] == "s1")
        & (evaluator.metrics["dataset"] == "d1")
        & (evaluator.metrics["cv_fold"] == 0)
    ]
    assert perfect["mae_mean"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(0.0)
    assert perfect["mae_stderr"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(0.0)


def test_evaluate_aggregates_over_folds_per_dataset(evaluator):
    """``metrics_by_strategy_dataset`` averages over folds only."""
    by_dataset = evaluator.metrics_by_strategy_dataset.set_index(
        ["dataset", "strategy"]
    )

    assert len(by_dataset) == len(STRATEGIES) * len(DATASETS)
    assert "cv_fold" not in by_dataset.columns
    for key, expected in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_DATASET.items():
        assert by_dataset.loc[key, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_evaluate_single_cv_fold_only_uses_that_fold(results):
    """Passing an integer ``cv_fold`` restricts the computation to that fold."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    aggregated = ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), cv_fold=1)

    assert set(ev.metrics["cv_fold"]) == {1}
    assert len(ev.metrics) == len(STRATEGIES) * len(DATASETS)

    by_dataset = ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset.set_index(["dataset", "strategy"])
    for key, per_fold in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD.items():
        assert by_dataset.loc[key, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(per_fold[1])
    assert set(aggregated["strategy"]) == set(STRATEGIES)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("cv_fold", [-1, "invalid", 1.5, None])
def test_evaluate_invalid_cv_fold_raises(results, cv_fold):
    """Non integer/non ``'all'`` ``cv_fold`` values are rejected."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="`cv_fold` must be either"):
        ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), cv_fold=cv_fold)


def test_evaluate_without_cv_splits_raises():
    """``cv_fold='all'`` on a splitter without splits is an error."""
    res = _build_results(n_splits=0)
    ev = _new_evaluator(res)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), cv_fold="all")


def test_evaluate_can_select_train_predictions():
    """``train_or_test`` selects which stored predictions are evaluated."""
    res = _build_results(with_train=True)

    test_evaluator = _new_evaluator(res)
    test_evaluator.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), train_or_test="test")

    train_evaluator = _new_evaluator(res)
    train_evaluator.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), train_or_test="train")

    assert train_evaluator.metrics_by_strategy["mae_mean"].tolist() == pytest.approx(
        [TRAIN_MAE] * len(STRATEGIES)
    )
    assert test_evaluator.metrics_by_strategy.set_index("strategy").loc[
        "s1", "mae_mean"
    ] == pytest.approx(EXPECTED_MAE_PER_STRATEGY["s1"])


def test_evaluate_supports_multiple_metrics(results):
    """A second metric is merged next to the first one."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric())
    aggregated = ev.evaluate(metric=_maxae_metric())

    assert ev.metric_names == ["mae", "maxae"]
    assert list(aggregated.columns) == [
        "strategy",
        "mae_mean",
        "mae_stderr",
        "maxae_mean",
        "maxae_stderr",
    ]
    assert list(ev.metrics.columns) == [
        "dataset",
        "strategy",
        "cv_fold",
        "mae_mean",
        "mae_stderr",
        "maxae_mean",
        "maxae_stderr",
    ]

    by_strategy = aggregated.set_index("strategy")
    assert by_strategy.loc["s2", "maxae_mean"] == pytest.approx(
        float(np.mean([EXPECTED_MAXAE_PER_DATASET[("s2", "d1")],
                       EXPECTED_MAXAE_PER_DATASET[("s2", "d2")]]))
    )
    for key, expected in EXPECTED_MAXAE_PER_DATASET.items():
        row = ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset[
            (ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset["strategy"] == key[0])
            & (ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset["dataset"] == key[1])
        ]
        assert row["maxae_mean"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_metric_name_defaults_to_function_name(results):
    """A metric without explicit ``name`` is registered under its function name."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        metric = PairwiseMetric(func=_mean_absolute_error)

    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    aggregated = ev.evaluate(metric=metric)

    assert ev.metric_names == ["_mean_absolute_error"]
    assert "mae" not in aggregated.columns
    assert "_mean_absolute_error_mean" in aggregated.columns


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# private helper behaviour reached through public entry points
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_column_names_follow_metric_and_suffix_convention(evaluator):
    """Metric columns are ``<metric>_mean`` / ``<metric>_stderr``."""
    assert evaluator._get_column_name("my_metric") == "my_metric_mean"
    assert evaluator._get_column_name("my_metric", suffix="stderr") == (
        "my_metric_stderr"
    )


def test_unknown_metric_name_is_rejected(evaluator):
    """A metric which was never evaluated cannot be used downstream."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="has not been evaluated yet"):
        evaluator.rank(metric_name="not-a-metric")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="has not been evaluated yet"):
        evaluator.t_test(metric_name="not-a-metric")


def test_metric_name_none_uses_last_evaluated_metric(results):
    """``metric_name=None`` falls back to the most recently evaluated metric."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric())
    ev.evaluate(metric=_maxae_metric())

    ranked = ev.rank()
    assert list(ranked.columns) == ["strategy", "maxae_mean_rank"]

    ranked_first = ev.rank(metric_name="mae")
    assert list(ranked_first.columns) == ["strategy", "mae_mean_rank"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ranking
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_rank_of_higher_metric_values_first(evaluator):
    """With ``ascending=False`` the largest metric value ranks first."""
    ranked = evaluator.rank(ascending=False).set_index("strategy")

points.  Real repository collaborators (``RAMResults``, ``PairwiseMetric``)
are used throughout; only the (fixed) seed data, the cross validation
splitter and, where unavoidable, the plotting backends are controlled.
"""

import importlib.util
import itertools
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from sktime.benchmarking.evaluation import Evaluator
from sktime.benchmarking.metrics import PairwiseMetric
from sktime.benchmarking.results import RAMResults
from sktime.exceptions import NotEvaluatedError

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# deterministic fixture data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Y_TRUE = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])

STRATEGIES = ("s1", "s2", "s3")
DATASETS = ("d1", "d2")
FOLDS = (0, 1)

# predictions per (strategy, dataset), one array per cv fold
PREDICTIONS = {
    ("s1", "d1"): [[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 6.0]],
    ("s1", "d2"): [[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], [2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0]],
    ("s2", "d1"): [[2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0], [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]],
    ("s2", "d2"): [[1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 3.0], [2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0]],
    ("s3", "d1"): [[1.5, 3.0, 4.0, 4.5], [2.0, 3.5, 4.5, 5.0]],
    ("s3", "d2"): [[2.0, 3.5, 4.5, 5.0], [1.5, 3.0, 4.0, 4.5]],
}

# hand-computed mean absolute error of the predictions above, per fold
EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD = {
    ("s1", "d1"): (0.0, 0.5),
    ("s1", "d2"): (0.0, 1.0),
    ("s2", "d1"): (1.0, 1.5),
    ("s2", "d2"): (0.5, 1.0),
    ("s3", "d1"): (0.75, 1.25),
    ("s3", "d2"): (1.25, 0.75),
}

# hand-computed average of the fold values above
EXPECTED_MAE_PER_DATASET = {
    key: float(np.mean(values)) for key, values in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD.items()
}

# hand-computed average of the per-dataset values above
EXPECTED_MAE_PER_STRATEGY = {
    strategy: float(
        np.mean(
            [
                EXPECTED_MAE_PER_DATASET[(strategy, dataset)]
                for dataset in DATASETS
            ]
        )
    )
    for strategy in STRATEGIES
}

# hand-computed mean absolute error of the max-absolute-error metric, per fold
EXPECTED_MAXAE_PER_DATASET = {
    ("s1", "d1"): 1.0,
    ("s1", "d2"): 0.5,
    ("s2", "d1"): 2.5,
    ("s2", "d2"): 0.5,
    ("s3", "d1"): 1.25,
    ("s3", "d2"): 1.25,
}

FIT_SECONDS = {0: 10.0, 1: 20.0}
PREDICT_SECONDS = {0: 5.0, 1: 10.0}
MEAN_FIT_SECONDS = float(np.mean(list(FIT_SECONDS.values())))
MEAN_PREDICT_SECONDS = float(np.mean(list(PREDICT_SECONDS.values())))

# constant predictions used for the "train" split, MAE with Y_TRUE is 2.5
TRAIN_Y_PRED = np.zeros(4)
TRAIN_MAE = 2.5


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class _FixedCV:
    """Minimal deterministic stand-in for a cross validation splitter."""

    def __init__(self, n_splits):
        self._n_splits = n_splits

    def get_n_splits(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return self._n_splits


def _mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred):
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    return float(np.mean(np.abs(y_true - y_pred)))


def _max_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred):
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)
    y_pred = np.asarray(y_pred, dtype=float)
    return float(np.max(np.abs(y_true - y_pred)))


def _build_results(
    strategies=STRATEGIES,
    datasets=DATASETS,
    folds=FOLDS,
    n_splits=2,
    with_train=False,
):
    """Build an in-memory ``RAMResults`` with deterministic predictions."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        results = RAMResults()
    results.cv = _FixedCV(n_splits=n_splits)

    for strategy, dataset in itertools.product(strategies, datasets):
        for fold in folds:
            fit_start = pd.Timestamp("2020-01-01 00:00:00")
            fit_end = fit_start + pd.Timedelta(seconds=FIT_SECONDS[fold])
            predict_start = fit_end
            predict_end = predict_start + pd.Timedelta(seconds=PREDICT_SECONDS[fold])
            timings = {
                "fit_estimator_start_time": fit_start,
                "fit_estimator_end_time": fit_end,
                "predict_estimator_start_time": predict_start,
                "predict_estimator_end_time": predict_end,
            }
            with warnings.catch_warnings():
                warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
                results.save_predictions(
                    strategy_name=strategy,
                    dataset_name=dataset,
                    y_true=Y_TRUE,
                    y_pred=np.array(PREDICTIONS[(strategy, dataset)][fold]),
                    y_proba=None,
                    index=np.arange(len(Y_TRUE)),
                    cv_fold=fold,
                    train_or_test="test",
                    **timings,
                )
                if with_train:
                    results.save_predictions(
                        strategy_name=strategy,
                        dataset_name=dataset,
                        y_true=Y_TRUE,
                        y_pred=TRAIN_Y_PRED,
                        y_proba=None,
                        index=np.arange(len(Y_TRUE)),
                        cv_fold=fold,
                        train_or_test="train",
                        **timings,
                    )
    return results


def _new_evaluator(results):
    """Create an ``Evaluator`` without surfacing the deprecation warning."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        return Evaluator(results)


def _mae_metric():
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        return PairwiseMetric(func=_mean_absolute_error, name="mae")


def _maxae_metric():
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        return PairwiseMetric(func=_max_absolute_error, name="maxae")


@pytest.fixture
def results():
    """In-memory results for three strategies, two datasets and two folds."""
    return _build_results()


@pytest.fixture
def raw_evaluator(results):
    """Evaluator that has not computed any metric yet."""
    return _new_evaluator(results)


@pytest.fixture
def evaluator(results):
    """Evaluator with the ``mae`` metric computed on all folds."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric())
    return ev


@pytest.fixture
def plot_backend(monkeypatch):
    """Run the legacy plotting helpers on current matplotlib/numpy.

    ``plot_boxplots`` asks for the ``seaborn-ticks`` style which matplotlib
    renamed to ``seaborn-v0_8-ticks`` and the critical difference diagram
    relies on ``numpy.asfarray`` which was removed in numpy 2.  Both are
    external compatibility shims, not changes to the behaviour under test.
    """
    matplotlib = pytest.importorskip("matplotlib")
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    legacy_style_use = plt.style.use

    def _style_use(style):
        if style == "seaborn-ticks" and style not in plt.style.available:
            style = "seaborn-v0_8-ticks"
        return legacy_style_use(style)

    monkeypatch.setattr(plt.style, "use", _style_use)
    if not hasattr(np, "asfarray"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(np, "asfarray", np.asarray, raising=False)
    yield plt
    plt.close("all")

def test_evaluator_requires_base_results():
    """Passing a non-``BaseResults`` object is rejected."""
    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="must inherit from BaseResults"):
            Evaluator(results=[1, 2, 3])


def test_evaluator_emits_v1_deprecation_warning():
    """The deprecated v1 evaluator warns on construction."""
    res = _build_results()
    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning, match="deprecated"):
        ev = Evaluator(res)
    assert ev.results is res


def test_metric_names_is_empty_before_evaluation(raw_evaluator):
    """``metric_names`` is readable (and empty) on an unevaluated evaluator."""
    assert raw_evaluator.metric_names == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "attribute",
    ["metrics", "metrics_by_strategy", "metrics_by_strategy_dataset"],
)
def test_metrics_properties_require_evaluation(raw_evaluator, attribute):

def test_evaluate_returns_aggregated_metrics_by_strategy(evaluator):
    """``evaluate`` returns (and exposes) the per-strategy aggregation."""
    aggregated = evaluator.metrics_by_strategy

    pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(aggregated, evaluator.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric()))

    assert list(aggregated.columns) == ["strategy", "mae_mean", "mae_stderr"]
    assert set(aggregated["strategy"]) == set(STRATEGIES)
    assert evaluator.metric_names == ["mae"]


def test_evaluate_aggregates_metric_values_per_strategy(evaluator):
    """Per-strategy metric values are the mean over datasets and folds."""
    aggregated = evaluator.metrics_by_strategy.set_index("strategy")
    for strategy, expected in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_STRATEGY.items():
        assert aggregated.loc[strategy, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_evaluate_records_one_row_per_strategy_dataset_and_fold(evaluator):
    """Raw per-fold metrics are stored with the documented columns."""
    metrics = evaluator.metrics

    assert list(metrics.columns) == [
        "dataset",
        "strategy",
        "cv_fold",
        "mae_mean",
        "mae_stderr",
    ]
    assert len(metrics) == len(STRATEGIES) * len(DATASETS) * len(FOLDS)

    for (strategy, dataset), per_fold in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD.items():
        rows = metrics[
            (metrics["strategy"] == strategy) & (metrics["dataset"] == dataset)
        ].set_index("cv_fold")
        for fold, expected in enumerate(per_fold):
            assert rows.loc[fold, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_evaluate_stores_non_negative_standard_errors(evaluator):
    """The ``stderr`` companion column is populated for every fold."""
    stderrs = evaluator.metrics["mae_stderr"]
    assert stderrs.notna().all()
    assert (stderrs >= 0).all()
    # the degenerate fold with a perfect forecast has zero error spread
    perfect = evaluator.metrics[
        (evaluator.metrics["strategy"] == "s1")
        & (evaluator.metrics["dataset"] == "d1")
        & (evaluator.metrics["cv_fold"] == 0)
    ]
    assert perfect["mae_mean"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(0.0)
    assert perfect["mae_stderr"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(0.0)


def test_evaluate_aggregates_over_folds_per_dataset(evaluator):
    """``metrics_by_strategy_dataset`` averages over folds only."""
    by_dataset = evaluator.metrics_by_strategy_dataset.set_index(
        ["dataset", "strategy"]
    )

    assert len(by_dataset) == len(STRATEGIES) * len(DATASETS)
    assert "cv_fold" not in by_dataset.columns
    for key, expected in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_DATASET.items():
        assert by_dataset.loc[key, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_evaluate_single_cv_fold_only_uses_that_fold(results):
    """Passing an integer ``cv_fold`` restricts the computation to that fold."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    aggregated = ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), cv_fold=1)

    assert set(ev.metrics["cv_fold"]) == {1}
    assert len(ev.metrics) == len(STRATEGIES) * len(DATASETS)

    by_dataset = ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset.set_index(["dataset", "strategy"])
    for key, per_fold in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD.items():
        assert by_dataset.loc[key, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(per_fold[1])
    assert set(aggregated["strategy"]) == set(STRATEGIES)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("cv_fold", [-1, "invalid", 1.5, None])
def test_evaluate_invalid_cv_fold_raises(results, cv_fold):
    """Non integer/non ``'all'`` ``cv_fold`` values are rejected."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="`cv_fold` must be either"):
        ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), cv_fold=cv_fold)


def test_evaluate_without_cv_splits_raises():
    """``cv_fold='all'`` on a splitter without splits is an error."""
    res = _build_results(n_splits=0)
    ev = _new_evaluator(res)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), cv_fold="all")


def test_evaluate_can_select_train_predictions():
    """``train_or_test`` selects which stored predictions are evaluated."""
    res = _build_results(with_train=True)

    test_evaluator = _new_evaluator(res)
    test_evaluator.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), train_or_test="test")

    train_evaluator = _new_evaluator(res)
    train_evaluator.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), train_or_test="train")

    assert train_evaluator.metrics_by_strategy["mae_mean"].tolist() == pytest.approx(
        [TRAIN_MAE] * len(STRATEGIES)
    )
    assert test_evaluator.metrics_by_strategy.set_index("strategy").loc[
        "s1", "mae_mean"
    ] == pytest.approx(EXPECTED_MAE_PER_STRATEGY["s1"])


def test_evaluate_supports_multiple_metrics(results):
    """A second metric is merged next to the first one."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric())
    aggregated = ev.evaluate(metric=_maxae_metric())

    assert ev.metric_names == ["mae", "maxae"]
    assert list(aggregated.columns) == [
        "strategy",
        "mae_mean",
        "mae_stderr",
        "maxae_mean",
        "maxae_stderr",
    ]
    assert list(ev.metrics.columns) == [
        "dataset",
        "strategy",
        "cv_fold",
        "mae_mean",
        "mae_stderr",
        "maxae_mean",
        "maxae_stderr",
    ]

    by_strategy = aggregated.set_index("strategy")
    assert by_strategy.loc["s2", "maxae_mean"] == pytest.approx(
        float(np.mean([EXPECTED_MAXAE_PER_DATASET[("s2", "d1")],
                       EXPECTED_MAXAE_PER_DATASET[("s2", "d2")]]))
    )
    for key, expected in EXPECTED_MAXAE_PER_DATASET.items():
        row = ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset[
            (ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset["strategy"] == key[0])
            & (ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset["dataset"] == key[1])
        ]
        assert row["maxae_mean"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_metric_name_defaults_to_function_name(results):
    """A metric without explicit ``name`` is registered under its function name."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
        metric = PairwiseMetric(func=_mean_absolute_error)

    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    aggregated = ev.evaluate(metric=metric)

    assert ev.metric_names == ["_mean_absolute_error"]
    assert "mae" not in aggregated.columns

def test_unknown_metric_name_is_rejected(evaluator):
    """A metric which was never evaluated cannot be used downstream."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="has not been evaluated yet"):
        evaluator.rank(metric_name="not-a-metric")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="has not been evaluated yet"):

def test_metric_name_none_uses_last_evaluated_metric(results):
    """``metric_name=None`` falls back to the most recently evaluated metric."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric())
    ev.evaluate(metric=_maxae_metric())

    ranked = ev.rank()
    assert list(ranked.columns) == ["strategy", "maxae_mean_rank"]

    ranked_first = ev.rank(metric_name="mae")
    assert list(ranked_first.columns) == ["strategy", "mae_mean_rank"]

def test_rank_of_higher_metric_values_first(evaluator):
    """With ``ascending=False`` the largest metric value ranks first."""
    ranked = evaluator.rank(ascending=False).set_index("strategy")

    assert ranked.loc["s1", "mae_mean_rank"] == pytest.approx(3.0)
    assert ranked.loc["s2", "mae_mean_rank"] == pytest.approx(1.5)
    assert ranked.loc["s3", "mae_mean_rank"] == pytest.approx(1.5)


def test_rank_ascending_reverses_the_order(evaluator):
    """With ``ascending=True`` the smallest metric value ranks first."""
    ranked = evaluator.rank(ascending=True).set_index("strategy")

    assert ranked.loc["s1", "mae_mean_rank"] == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert ranked.loc["s2", "mae_mean_rank"] == pytest.approx(2.5)
    assert ranked.loc["s3", "mae_mean_rank"] == pytest.approx(2.5)


def test_rank_rejects_non_boolean_ascending(evaluator):
    """``ascending`` has to be a real boolean."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="`ascending` must be boolean"):
        evaluator.rank(ascending="yes")

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "method",
    [
        "rank",
        "t_test",
        "sign_test",
        "ranksum_test",
        "t_test_with_bonferroni_correction",
        "wilcoxon_test",
        "friedman_test",
    ],
)
def test_statistical_helpers_require_evaluation(raw_evaluator, method):
    """Statistical helpers refuse to run before a metric was evaluated."""
    with pytest.raises(NotEvaluatedError):
        getattr(raw_evaluator, method)()


def test_t_test_returns_pairwise_table_and_matrix(evaluator):
    """``t_test`` compares every ordered pair of strategies."""
    t_df, values_df = evaluator.t_test()

    assert list(t_df.columns) == ["estimator_1", "estimator_2", "t_stat", "p_val"]
    assert len(t_df) == len(STRATEGIES) ** 2
    assert set(zip(t_df["estimator_1"], t_df["estimator_2"])) == set(
        itertools.product(STRATEGIES, STRATEGIES)
    )

    # self comparisons of identical samples give undefined statistics
    diagonal = t_df[t_df["estimator_1"] == t_df["estimator_2"]]
    assert diagonal["t_stat"].isna().all()

    # the pairwise statistic is antisymmetric
    s1_s2 = t_df[(t_df["estimator_1"] == "s1") & (t_df["estimator_2"] == "s2")]
    s2_s1 = t_df[(t_df["estimator_1"] == "s2") & (t_df["estimator_2"] == "s1")]
    assert s1_s2["t_stat"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(-s2_s1["t_stat"].iloc[0])
    assert s1_s2["p_val"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(s2_s1["p_val"].iloc[0])

    assert values_df.shape == (len(STRATEGIES), 2 * len(STRATEGIES))
    assert list(values_df.index) == list(STRATEGIES)
    assert values_df.columns.get_level_values(1).unique().tolist() == [
        "t_stat",
        "p_val",
    ]
    assert values_df.loc["s1", ("s2", "p_val")] == pytest.approx(
        s1_s2["p_val"].iloc[0]
    )


def test_sign_test_returns_table_and_pivot(evaluator):
    """``sign_test`` reports binomial p-values for all ordered pairs."""
    sign_df, pivot = evaluator.sign_test()

    assert list(sign_df.columns) == ["estimator_1", "estimator_2", "p_val"]
    assert len(sign_df) == len(STRATEGIES) ** 2
    assert ((sign_df["p_val"] >= 0) & (sign_df["p_val"] <= 1)).all()

    assert pivot.shape == (len(STRATEGIES), len(STRATEGIES))
    assert list(pivot.index) == list(STRATEGIES)
    assert list(pivot.columns) == list(STRATEGIES)

    row = sign_df[(sign_df["estimator_1"] == "s1") & (sign_df["estimator_2"] == "s2")]
    assert pivot.loc["s1", "s2"] == pytest.approx(row["p_val"].iloc[0])


def test_ranksum_test_returns_pairwise_table_and_matrix(evaluator):
    """``ranksum_test`` reports Wilcoxon rank-sum statistics."""
    ranksum_df, values_df = evaluator.ranksum_test()

    assert list(ranksum_df.columns) == [
        "estimator_1",
        "estimator_2",
        "t_stat",
        "p_val",
    ]
    assert len(ranksum_df) == len(STRATEGIES) ** 2
    assert ((ranksum_df["p_val"] >= 0) & (ranksum_df["p_val"] <= 1)).all()

    s1_s2 = ranksum_df[
        (ranksum_df["estimator_1"] == "s1") & (ranksum_df["estimator_2"] == "s2")
    ]
    s2_s1 = ranksum_df[
        (ranksum_df["estimator_1"] == "s2") & (ranksum_df["estimator_2"] == "s1")
    ]
    assert s1_s2["t_stat"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(-s2_s1["t_stat"].iloc[0])

    assert values_df.shape == (len(STRATEGIES), 2 * len(STRATEGIES))
    assert values_df.loc["s1", ("s1", "p_val")] == pytest.approx(1.0)


def test_wilcoxon_test_compares_unordered_pairs(evaluator):
    """``wilcoxon_test`` only compares each unordered pair once."""
    wilcoxon_df = evaluator.wilcoxon_test()

    assert list(wilcoxon_df.columns) == [
        "estimator_1",
        "estimator_2",
        "statistic",
        "p_val",
    ]
    assert len(wilcoxon_df) == 3
    assert set(zip(wilcoxon_df["estimator_1"], wilcoxon_df["estimator_2"])) == set(
        itertools.combinations(STRATEGIES, 2)
    )
    assert ((wilcoxon_df["p_val"] >= 0) & (wilcoxon_df["p_val"] <= 1)).all()
    assert wilcoxon_df["statistic"].notna().all()


def test_friedman_test_returns_result_and_table(evaluator):
    """``friedman_test`` returns the scipy result plus a summary frame."""
    result, values_df = evaluator.friedman_test()

    assert list(values_df.columns) == ["statistic", "p_value"]
    assert len(values_df) == 1
    assert values_df["statistic"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(float(result[0]))
    assert values_df["p_value"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(float(result[1]))
    assert 0.0 <= float(result[1]) <= 1.0


def test_friedman_test_requires_at_least_three_strategies():
    """The Friedman test is undefined for fewer than three strategies."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(_build_results(strategies=("s1", "s2")))
    ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric())
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ev.friedman_test()


def test_t_test_with_bonferroni_correction(evaluator):
    """Bonferroni correction flags p-values below ``alpha / n_comparisons``."""
    full_alpha = 0.05
    correctly_corrected = evaluator.t_test_with_bonferroni_correction(alpha=full_alpha)
    t_df, _ = evaluator.t_test()

    n_comparisons = len(STRATEGIES) ** 2

class _FixedCV:

    y_true = np.asarray(y_true, dtype=float)

            predict_start = fit_end
            predict_end = predict_start + pd.Timedelta(seconds=PREDICT_SECONDS[fold])
            timings = {

                "fit_estimator_end_time": fit_end,
                "predict_estimator_start_time": predict_start,
                "predict_estimator_end_time": predict_end,
            }
            with warnings.catch_warnings():

                results.save_predictions(
                    strategy_name=strategy,
                    dataset_name=dataset,
                    y_true=Y_TRUE,
                    y_pred=np.array(PREDICTIONS[(strategy, dataset)][fold]),
                    y_proba=None,
                    index=np.arange(len(Y_TRUE)),
                    cv_fold=fold,

        ["strategy", "dataset"]
    )

    assert len(by_dataset) == len(STRATEGIES) * len(DATASETS)
    assert "cv_fold" not in by_dataset.columns
    for key, expected in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_DATASET.items():

def test_evaluate_single_cv_fold_only_uses_that_fold(results):
    """Passing an integer ``cv_fold`` restricts the computation to that fold."""
    ev = _new_evaluator(results)
    aggregated = ev.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), cv_fold=1)

    assert set(ev.metrics["cv_fold"]) == {1}
    assert len(ev.metrics) == len(STRATEGIES) * len(DATASETS)

    by_dataset = ev.metrics_by_strategy_dataset.set_index(["strategy", "dataset"])
    for key, per_fold in EXPECTED_MAE_PER_FOLD.items():
        assert by_dataset.loc[key, "mae_mean"] == pytest.approx(per_fold[1])
    assert set(aggregated["strategy"]) == set(STRATEGIES)

    """``cv_fold='all'`` on a splitter without splits is an error."""

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):

def test_evaluate_can_select_train_predictions():
    """``train_or_test`` selects which stored predictions are evaluated."""
    res = _build_results(with_train=True)

    test_evaluator = _new_evaluator(res)
    test_evaluator.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), train_or_test="test")

    train_evaluator = _new_evaluator(res)
    train_evaluator.evaluate(metric=_mae_metric(), train_or_test="train")

    assert train_evaluator.metrics_by_strategy["mae_mean"].tolist() == pytest.approx(

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from sktime.libs.kronos.module import (
    BSQuantizer,
    DependencyAwareLayer,
    DualHead,
    HierarchicalEmbedding,
    RMSNorm,

    TransformerBlock,
)
from sktime.utils.dependencies import _safe_import

trange = _safe_import("tqdm.trange")
torch = _safe_import("torch")
nn = _safe_import("torch.nn", return_object="None")
F = _safe_import("torch.nn.functional")

if nn is None:

    class _DummyModule:
        pass

    class nn:
        Module = _DummyModule


PyTorchModelHubMixin = _safe_import(
    "huggingface_hub.PyTorchModelHubMixin",
    pkg_name="huggingface_hub",
    return_object="None",
)

if PyTorchModelHubMixin is None:

    class PyTorchModelHubMixin:
        def __init_subclass__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
            pass


__all__ = [
    "Kronos",
    "KronosPredictor",
    "KronosTokenizer",
    "auto_regressive_inference",
    "calc_time_stamps",
    "sample_from_logits",
    "top_k_top_p_filtering",
]


class KronosTokenizer(nn.Module, PyTorchModelHubMixin):
    """Tokenize K-line features with binary spherical quantization."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        d_in,
        d_model,
        n_heads,
        ff_dim,
        n_enc_layers,
        n_dec_layers,
        ffn_dropout_p,
        attn_dropout_p,
        resid_dropout_p,
        s1_bits,
        s2_bits,
        beta,
        gamma0,
        gamma,
        zeta,
        group_size,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.d_in = d_in
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.ff_dim = ff_dim
        self.enc_layers = n_enc_layers
        self.dec_layers = n_dec_layers
        self.ffn_dropout_p = ffn_dropout_p
        self.attn_dropout_p = attn_dropout_p
        self.resid_dropout_p = resid_dropout_p

        self.s1_bits = s1_bits
        self.s2_bits = s2_bits
        self.codebook_dim = (
            s1_bits + s2_bits
        )  # Total dimension of the codebook after quantization
        self.embed = nn.Linear(self.d_in, self.d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(self.d_model, self.d_in)

        # Encoder Transformer Blocks
        self.encoder = nn.ModuleList(
            [
                TransformerBlock(

        gamma,

        group_size,
    ):

            [
                TransformerBlock(
                    self.d_model,
                    self.n_heads,

                    self.resid_dropout_p,
                )
                for _ in range(self.enc_layers - 1)
            ]
        )

        self.decoder = nn.ModuleList(
            [
                TransformerBlock(
                    self.d_model,
                    self.n_heads,
                    self.ff_dim,
                    self.ffn_dropout_p,
                    self.attn_dropout_p,
                    self.resid_dropout_p,

                for _ in range(self.dec_layers - 1)

            in_features=self.d_model, out_features=self.codebook_dim
        )  # Linear layer before quantization
        self.post_quant_embed_pre = nn.Linear(
            in_features=self.s1_bits, out_features=self.d_model
        )  # Linear layer after quantization (pre part - s1 bits)
        self.post_quant_embed = nn.Linear(
            in_features=self.codebook_dim, out_features=self.d_model
        )  # Linear layer after quantization (full codebook)

            self.s1_bits, self.s2_bits, beta, gamma0, gamma, zeta, group_size

    def indices_to_bits(self, x, half=False):

        if half:
            x1 = x[0]  # Assuming x is a tuple of indices if half is True
            x2 = x[1]
            mask = 2 ** torch.arange(
                self.codebook_dim // 2, device=x1.device, dtype=torch.long
            )  # Create a mask for bit extraction
            x1 = (x1.unsqueeze(-1) & mask) != 0  # Extract bits for the first half
            x2 = (x2.unsqueeze(-1) & mask) != 0  # Extract bits for the second half

        quantized = self.indices_to_bits(x, half)
        z = self.post_quant_embed(quantized)
        for layer in self.decoder:
            z = layer(z)
        z = self.head(z)
        return z

                    self.d_model,

                    self.resid_dropout_p,

    def _init_weights(self, module):

                nn.init.zeros_(module.bias)
        elif isinstance(module, nn.Embedding):
            nn.init.normal_(module.weight, mean=0, std=self.embedding.d_model**-0.5)
        elif isinstance(module, nn.LayerNorm):
